book.edition: James Joyce, Ulysses — Standard Ebooks edition (released to the public domain, CC0; see uncopyright.xhtml)
book.structure: 25 spine items, one per NCX navPoint; NCX nests chapters under Parts I-III. Chapters XII, XIV, XVI, XVII, XVIII split into 2 chunks and XV into 7 (Moon+ 10.8 rule, 100,000-char body).

device: Samsung Galaxy S25 (SM-S931B), Android 17, 1080x2340; Moon+ Reader Pro 10.8, automatic Drive sync
display: The user's Moon+ display settings, unchanged (dark theme, justified text with hyphenation, status line on).
notes: Chapter index = flattened NCX ordinal = spine index for this book (one navPoint per spine file); Parts are their own chapters (index 2, 6, 19).

Split boundaries match A.createSplitHtmls on the <body> inner HTML: cut at the next '<p' within 20,000 chars of 100,000, else after the next '>'. XV chunk @3 starts mid-paragraph ('He touches the keys again.') because the next '<p' was beyond the 20,000 window: Moon+ cut after the opening <i ...> tag.
Offsets restart at 0 in every chunk: the .po at a chunk's first page is {chapter}@{split}#0 and a probe on its first character is at position 0.
Moon+ draws a '[n/N]' marker (blue, after a line break) at the end of every non-final chunk; it is part of the chunk's rendered text after the last character.
The status line's page numbers are estimates across chunks (the same page showed 1/24, 41/58 and 49/147-style counts); only the .po is reliable.

A forced 'Sync to cloud' right after a chapter-list jump or a backward page turn uploaded a stale offset (chapter start, offset 0); closing the reader uploaded the real position. Captures here use close.
Moon+'s word selection treats the curly apostrophe as a word break: long-pressing "I’m" selected from 'm'.
